clue.text: Promissory note accepted by north London outfit is false

indicators.note: something accepted by a group is taken in among them, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a north London football club
an IOU is a written promise to pay a debt

explanation.surface: An IOU taken by a London football club turns out to be worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: Tottenham Hotspur, known as Spurs, is a football club in north London.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spurious is fake or not genuine, a synonym of false.

clue.text: You find it in the upper part of the wood

definitions.text: You find it in the upper part of the wood

parts.words: You find it in the upper part of the wood
parts.note: the wood suggests a forest canopy, but it is the orchestra's woodwind section, and the instrument meant plays its highest notes

explanation.surface: A riddle about something living high in the trees of a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The wood' is short for the woodwind; the small flute sits at the top of its range.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest flute is pitched an octave above the ordinary flute, the highest member of the woodwind family.

clue.text: Orange river I'd crossed -it forms part of the state border

definitions.text: it forms part of the state border

indicators.note: letters crossed over one another are mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: An explorer crosses a river that marks the edge of a state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossed' shuffles ORANGE, R and ID. The river named runs along the Texas boundary with Mexico.
explanation.definitionFit: This North American river marks the frontier between Texas and Mexico for much of its course.

clue.text: Power associated with logarithm, frequently

definitions.meaning: common logarithms are to base ten, so the power is one ..., read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words the first gives the base of common logarithms, a power 'of ten'; as one word it is a synonym of many times.

clue.text: Being hard at it from the crack of dawn?

definitions.text: Being hard at it from the crack of dawn?

parts.words: Being hard at it from the crack of dawn?
parts.note: the surface is a worker up early, but read as a sector of the economy it is a new business that is just rising and growing fast

explanation.surface: Praise for someone who starts work at first light.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase names a new, fast-growing industry; the clue reads it as a trade carried on at daybreak.
explanation.definitionFit: A booming new branch of the economy is called this, punning on the sun coming up at dawn.

clue.text: Police involved in sec-end series of exercises in wood

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second

indicators.note: something involved in another is wrapped up inside it

parts.note: PE is physical education, a session of exercises at school
the RUC was the Royal Ulster Constabulary, the police force of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Officers join a quick workout in the forest.
explanation.walkthrough: RUC was the Royal Ulster Constabulary, the Northern Ireland police force; PE is school physical education.
explanation.definitionFit: This conifer gives a light timber widely used in building and for instruments.

clue.text: Attempt at concealment after spilling the salt

indicators.note: salt that is spilt scatters its grains, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tries to hide the fact that they knocked over the salt cellar.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting secretly to avoid being noticed is moving by furtive means.

clue.text: Weapon conveyed in sack

definitions.meaning: to plunder or ransack a place

explanation.surface: A gun carried hidden in a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a shoulder-fired gun; the verb means to ransack or search through and steal.

clue.text: House army supremo in church — it's cold and dark

indicators.note: one piece set in another goes inside it

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
CIC is commander-in-chief, the head of an army

explanation.surface: A general is housed in a church, which is chilly and gloomy.
explanation.definitionFit: This frozen dessert is a block of ice cream coated in dark chocolate, so it is chilly and dark.

clue.text: Content of programme chosen -repeat

indicators.note: the content of the words is what lies inside them, so the letters are taken from within

explanation.surface: A rerun of a selected broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflected sound repeats what was said, and to say again is the verb sense.

clue.text: Callow youth in bid to join infantry

indicators.note: one piece joins on to the next, side by side

parts.note: a tender is a formal offer or bid
foot soldiers are the infantry

explanation.surface: A young recruit makes an offer to enlist in the army.
explanation.definitionFit: A newcomer with no experience is a raw beginner, from the name once given to new settlers.

clue.text: Easily managed trailer, not very heavy

indicators.note: letters easily managed are handled and moved about freely into a new order

explanation.surface: A light trailer that is simple to tow.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain that pours down hard is described this way, so it means extremely heavy.

clue.text: Arrange for woman to leave hospital

indicators.note: a letter that leaves the word is dropped from it

parts.note: Edith is a woman's name
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Organising for a female patient to be discharged.
explanation.definitionFit: To prepare and put text in order for publication is to arrange it.

clue.text: Nag, one taking part in fox-hunt

definitions.meaning: to pester or harass someone persistently
a dog of the pack that chases the fox

explanation.surface: A horse ridden in a fox-hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nag' looks like a horse, which belongs in a hunt; here it is the verb to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to harass relentlessly; the noun is a hunting dog in the pack.

clue.text: Where one would expect to find his nibs?

definitions.text: Where one would expect to find his nibs?

parts.words: Where one would expect to find his nibs?
parts.note: 'his nibs' is a mocking name for a self-important man, but literally nibs are the points of writing instruments, kept in a stem

explanation.surface: Asking where a pompous boss is likely to be found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His nibs' is a British joke title for a self-important person; a nib is the metal point of a dip pen.
explanation.definitionFit: The stem or handle into which a metal writing point is fitted holds the nibs.

clue.text: Boy receiving a punch, staggering around plat form

indicators.note: a piece receiving another takes it inside

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: someone staggering around reels unsteadily, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A boy takes a blow and reels about on a stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staggering around' looks like it describes the boy reeling from the blow, but it is the anagram signal on the punch alone; 'receiving' then puts the a and the jumbled letters inside the boy.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocket lifts off from this base, a platform built for take-off.

clue.text: Leave after entering rowdy scene, making no trouble

indicators.note: the leaving word has something entering it, so the second piece goes inside

parts.note: to quit is to leave

indicators.note: a rowdy crowd is disorderly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone walks out of a noisy scene so as not to stir things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rowdy' jumbles the scene, and 'after entering' means the leaving word has that jumble inside it; 'making no trouble' is the definition, not part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dormant and inactive, at rest, means causing no disturbance.

clue.text: Free from restraint, pawnbroker with money gives away a couple of hundred

indicators.note: letters given away are removed

parts.note: 'uncle' is old slang for a pawnbroker
cash is money
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so two of them is CC

explanation.surface: A pawnbroker with cash hands over two hundred to let someone go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives away' removes the C from UNCLE and the C from CASH.
explanation.definitionFit: To let loose, as a dog off its lead, is to free it from restraint.

clue.text: Stronghold in which army's besieged by El Cid, maybe

indicators.note: something besieged is surrounded, so it goes inside
'maybe' says the letters could be some other arrangement

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force

explanation.surface: A fortress whose garrison is surrounded by the Spanish hero El Cid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges EL CID into CIDEL, which wraps TA. El Cid was a medieval Spanish warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortress commanding a city is a stronghold.

clue.text: Note objection about plant's store of reserves

indicators.note: turned about means turned round, so the joined pieces are read backwards

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a 'but' is an objection

explanation.surface: A botanist notes an objection about how a plant stores food.
explanation.definitionFit: A swollen underground stem, like a potato, stores food for the plant.

clue.text: Essayist takes an age penning document about queen

indicators.note: penning something encloses it, as in a pen

parts.note: an eon is an age

indicators.note: MS goes about ER, around it

parts.note: MS is a manuscript
ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A writer spends ages drafting a paper about a queen.
explanation.walkthrough: MS goes about ER to make MERS, and EON pens that.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo Emerson was the American writer famed for his essays.

clue.text: Thick slice of cake is left by sailor

parts.note: is shortened to 's
AB is an able seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor leaves a chunk of cake behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' gives S, as in the contraction 's.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick flat piece of something is a chunk.

clue.text: Bishop not so frequently having to pronounce benediction over

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bishop in chess
less is the opposite of more, so to a smaller degree

explanation.surface: A bishop rarely needs to say grace.
explanation.definitionFit: To invoke divine favour on someone is to give a benediction.

clue.text: Old means of persuading seamen to use hitches, initially

indicators.note: one piece placed initially comes first in the answer

parts.note: a hitchhiker thumbs a lift, so to hitch is to thumb
seamen form a ship's crew

explanation.surface: Sailors told to tie knots in the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' puts THUMBS first. 'Hitches' looks like knots but is hitchhiking.
explanation.definitionFit: This instrument of torture crushed the digits to extract confessions, a grim means of coercion.

clue.text: Fail to justify religious opinion, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means most of it, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a belief is a religious opinion

explanation.surface: A faith that cannot be fully justified.
explanation.definitionFit: To contradict or fail to fulfil an expectation is to fail to justify it.

clue.text: Set out with ill-assorted carload of priests

indicators.note: letters set out are laid in new places
an ill-assorted group is a jumble, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A car crammed with a motley group of clergy sets off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' and 'ill-assorted' mix SET and CARLOAD together.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes the priesthood and its functions, so it means priestly.

clue.text: Press husband to make an end of the matter

indicators.note: the husband makes the end of the next piece, so it goes last

parts.note: pus is matter discharged from a wound

explanation.surface: Urging a husband to finish the business.
explanation.definitionFit: To press means to shove or urge forward.

clue.text: Woodcutter from Switzerland is found lying beside railway

parts.note: CH is the international code for Switzerland
an el is an elevated railway

explanation.surface: A Swiss lumberjack found lying by the tracks.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpenter's edged tool cuts and shapes timber.

clue.text: Soft furnishing

definitions.meaning: producing or supplying, as a crop provides

explanation.surface: Cushions and upholstery.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means pliant under pressure; the verb form means producing or supplying.
